info.title: AutoElevate Partner API (Beta)
info.description:
The Partner API enables integration partners to programmatically access
AutoElevate data for their managed customers — usage metrics, computer
inventory, security events, and more.

## Beta

This API is in **beta** and may change without notice. Every request
must include an explicit acknowledgment header:

```
X-Acknowledgment: i-understand-this-is-beta-and-may-change
```

Requests missing this header — or sending any other value — are
rejected with **400 Bad Request**.

## Versioning

Every endpoint is versioned in its URL path — `/api/v1/computers`,
`/api/v2/computers`, and so on. Pin your integration to an explicit
version.

The **unversioned** path (`/api/computers`) is a permanent alias for
**v1** — never the latest version — so publishing a new version can
never silently change the behavior of an existing integration. New
versions are strictly opt-in: adopt one by changing the version segment
in the URL.

When a version is deprecated its responses carry a `Deprecation: true`
header and, once a removal date is committed, an RFC 8594 `Sunset`
header with that date; a `Link` header with `rel="successor-version"`
points at the replacement. A version is only removed after a published
deprecation window — watch for these headers to migrate ahead of time.

## Getting Started

### 1. Create an API Key

In the AutoElevate admin portal, open a **service user** and add an
**API Key**. Pick a scheme at creation time:

- **API Token (AE-BEARER)** — recommended for most integrations. Works
  with any HTTP client, iPaaS platform, SDK generator, or LLM tool.
- **HMAC (AE-HMAC-SHA256)** — request-signed scheme. Signs
  `scheme + METHOD + URL + bodyHash + ts`, so both the request
  target and the body are tamper-protected, bounded by a 5-minute
  replay window (see below for the exact signing steps).

Bearer keys show a single secret at creation. HMAC keys show **two**
values — a wire `token` and a separate `hmacKey` signing key —
both displayed once and never retrievable again.

### 2. Authenticate

**Bearer (AE-BEARER)** — send the token directly:

```bash
curl https://partner-api.autoelevate.com/api/usage \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer aeb_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx" \
  -H "X-Acknowledgment: i-understand-this-is-beta-and-may-change"
```

**HMAC (AE-HMAC-SHA256)** — request-signed scheme. Build the
`Authorization` header yourself:

1. Compute `bodyHash` — the SHA-256 hex digest of the exact request
   body bytes. For a request with no body (GET, or a write with an
   empty body), use the SHA-256 of the empty string:
   `e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855`
   — safe to hardcode rather than recompute every time.
2. Build the string to sign, joining the parts below with a real
   newline character (not the literal characters `\n`):

   ```
   AE-HMAC-SHA256
   <METHOD>
   <URL>
   <bodyHash>
   <ts>
   ```

   `<METHOD>` is uppercase (`GET`, `POST`, ...); `<URL>` is the
   full request target including any query string; `<ts>` is the
   current time as epoch milliseconds.
3. Compute `sig` — HMAC-SHA256 of that string using `hmacKey` as
   the key, hex-encoded.
4. Send the header:

```bash
curl https://partner-api.autoelevate.com/api/usage \
  -H "Authorization: AE-HMAC-SHA256 token=aeh_xxx,bodyHash=<hex>,ts=<epochMs>,sig=<hex>" \
  -H "X-Acknowledgment: i-understand-this-is-beta-and-may-change"
```

`ts` must be within 5 minutes of server time or the request is
rejected.

### 3. Keep Your Keys Safe

- **Prefer short-lived keys.** Expiration presets go down to 15
  minutes — for ad-hoc testing, shared machines, or any less-trusted
  environment, create a short-lived key instead of reusing a
  long-lived one.
- **Scope to least privilege.** Grant only the permissions the
  integration actually needs; avoid Full access keys for anything
  long-lived.
- **Store keys in a secrets manager** — never in source control,
  tickets, chat, or shared documents. If a key is ever exposed,
  revoke it immediately in the admin portal and create a new one.
- **Rotate on personnel or role changes.** Keys are tied to the
  service user they were created under; revoke keys that are no
  longer needed.

## Rate Limits

Limits are applied **per MSP, per HTTP method, per route path** —
each unique combination has its own bucket. Defaults during beta:

| Bucket | Limit |
|--------|-------|
| Most endpoints | 100 requests per hour |
| `/api/usage` | 100 requests per hour |

There is no separate per-minute burst layer today; the bucket
counter is a single sliding window. When rate-limited, the API
returns **429 Too Many Requests** with a `Retry-After` header.
Defaults are conservative for beta and may rise as the surface
stabilises.

## Client Libraries

Generate a client from the OpenAPI spec:

```bash
npx @openapitools/openapi-generator-cli generate \
  -i partners-openapi-spec.json \
  -g typescript-fetch -o ./partners-client-ts
```

BearerToken.description:
AutoElevate API key presented as a Bearer credential:

    Authorization: Bearer <token>

The key must be created with the **AE-BEARER** scheme in the
admin portal. Keys can carry an optional scope list that
narrows their effective permissions — see route-level
`security` for the scopes each endpoint accepts.

HmacSignature.name: Authorization
HmacSignature.description:
**Custom HMAC scheme.** Paste the full `Authorization`
header value, including the `AE-HMAC-SHA256` prefix and the
`token`, `bodyHash`, `ts`, and `sig` parameters you have
computed client-side. Off-the-shelf clients will not
auto-sign these requests; this entry exists so the spec
records that the API accepts this scheme alongside Bearer.

Wire format:

    Authorization: AE-HMAC-SHA256 token=<aeh_…>,bodyHash=<hex>,ts=<epochMs>,sig=<hex>

At key creation the admin portal shows **two** values:

- `token` — the wire identifier sent as `token=` on every
  request.
- `hmacKey` — the signing key. Kept client-side and never
  transmitted. Used to compute `sig` = HMAC-SHA256 over
  `AE-HMAC-SHA256\n<METHOD>\n<URL>\n<bodyHash>\n<ts>`,
  where `<URL>` is the full request target including any
  query string.

`bodyHash` is the SHA-256 hex digest of the exact request
body bytes. For a request with no body (GET, or a write
with an empty body), use the SHA-256 of the empty string:
`e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855`
— safe to hardcode rather than recompute every time.

`ts` must be within 5 minutes of server time or the request is
rejected.

The key must be created with the **AE-HMAC-SHA256** scheme
in the admin portal.

elevationType.description: Elevation level granted for the approval. `admin` performs the elevation with admin rights; `user` keeps the action at the user level. Optional — defaults to the request's existing elevation type.

createRule.description: When `true`, also create an auto-approval rule from this request so future matching elevations resolve automatically. Requires `ruleLevel`.

ruleLevel.description: Scope at which an auto-created rule applies: `computer`, `location`, `company`, or `msp` (all companies). Required when `createRule` is `true`.

durationInMinutes.description: For elevated-session requests, the length of the resulting session in minutes. Ignored for non-session requests.

id.description: Identifier of the user that performed the action.

type.description: Kind of actor. Currently always `human`: this feed only surfaces entries attributable to a user account.

name.description: The actor's current display name (a live lookup, not the name captured at the time of the event).

action.description: Normalized action, formatted `<entityType>.<verb>` where verb is one of `created`, `updated`, or `deleted`.

entityType.description: Type of object the action was performed on.

occurredAt.description: Time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

diff.description: Before/after payload. `{ after }` for a create, `{ before }` for a delete, `{ before, after }` for an update.

initials.description: Short form of the company name.

managementSystemCompanyId.description: External identifier the partner provided for this company. Defaults to the company name at creation when the partner supplies none; may be `null` for companies created through other paths.

createdAt.description: Time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

updatedAt.description: Time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

locationId.description: Location the computer is assigned to.

elevationMode.description: Effective elevation mode the agent last reported. `null` when the agent has not reported a recognized mode.

lastCheckedInAt.description: Most recent agent check-in. `null` when the computer has never reported in.

createdAt.description: Time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

updatedAt.description: Time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

createRule.description: When `true`, also create a denial rule from this request so future matching elevations are auto-denied. Requires `ruleLevel`.

ruleLevel.description: Scope at which an auto-created rule applies: `computer`, `location`, `company`, or `msp` (all companies). Required when `createRule` is `true`.

denialReason.description: Free-text reason for the denial, shown to the end user on their machine alongside the denial notification. Plain text; maximum 1000 characters.

userName.description: The OS user who held the elevated session, if known.

status.description: Lifecycle state of the elevated session.

startedAt.description: Time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

endedAt.description: The session's scheduled end time, epoch milliseconds. Set when the session is created and not updated if it ends early, so it reflects the scheduled — not necessarily the actual — end.

computerName.description: Friendly machine name of the computer at the time of the event.

companyName.description: Company that the computer belongs to.

trigger.description: The trigger that fired the event (path, file hash, signer, etc.). Shape varies by trigger source. `null` when the event carried no trigger.

user.description: The OS user that initiated the action; `null` when the event carried no user.

ruleThatApplied.description: The rule (if any) that matched at event time. `null` when no rule matched.

data.description: Minimal event payload exposed to partners. Detailed agent diagnostics are intentionally omitted.

createdAt.description: When the event was recorded by the API.

approvalState.description: Current approval state of the request.

requestedBy.description: OS user name that requested elevation, if known.

targetDescription.description: Short description of what is being elevated (e.g. "Install Foo.exe").

createdAt.description: Time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

denialReason.description: Free-text reason recorded when the request was denied, shown to the end user alongside the denial notification. Plain text. Present only when a denial reason was set.

mspId.description: MSP this rule applies to. Set when `level` is `msp`, otherwise `null`.

companyId.description: Company this rule applies to. Set when `level` is `company`, otherwise `null`.

locationId.description: Location this rule applies to. Set when `level` is `location`, otherwise `null`.

computerId.description: Computer this rule applies to. Set when `level` is `computer`, otherwise `null`.

approved.description: When `true`, matching elevations are auto-approved; when `false`, they are auto-denied.

shouldIgnore.description: When `true`, the agent treats matching events as audit-mode and does not prompt to elevate.

friendlyName.description: Optional human-readable name an admin set on the rule.

identificationCriteria.description: Opaque criteria the agent matches against incoming events to decide whether this rule applies. Shape is intentionally not part of the public contract — treat as a passthrough.

createdAt.description: Time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

updatedAt.description: Time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

ElevationRuleScope.description: Scope at which the elevation rule applies. Derived from which of `mspId`, `companyId`, `locationId`, or `computerId` is set on the underlying record.

get.description: Returns a keyset-paginated list of audit log entries scoped to the authenticated partner's MSP — use it for compliance reporting and QBR-style usage reconstruction. The feed currently covers **user** and **setting** changes; filter with `entityType` and `action`. Pass the `nextCursor` from each response back as `cursor` to page; results are bounded to the last 30 days.
